source_text:
πλάνην ἐρωτηθεὶς ὁ Χριστὸς ἔλεγεν· οὔτε οὗτος ἥμαρτεν οὔτε οἱ γονεῖς αὐτοῦ, ἀλλ'
ἵνα φανερωθῇ τὰ ἔργα θεοῦ.

1
thought_title: Christ answers the question and destroys the error
orientation: The author has just described the unlawful doctrine that souls are sent into bodies for punishment, and now quotes Christ's answer to the question about whose sin caused the condition.
pass_a_gloss: having been asked, Christ was saying, destroying such an error: neither this one sinned nor his parents, but in order that the works of God might be revealed.

choices.why: Glossary term for the false belief Christ destroys; keeps the abstract noun as object of the implied destroying.
Aorist passive participle; preserves the passive force and the temporal/causal nuance that Christ speaks in response to a question.
Imperfect indicative; keeps the ongoing or inceptive force of the direct speech introduction.
Correlative negation; preserves the paired negative structure exactly.

choices.english: in order that might be revealed
choices.why: Purpose clause with aorist passive subjunctive; keeps the purpose force and the passive voice.
Glossary term; keeps the exact phrase from the brief.

bible_refs.note: The quotation matches John 9:3 closely: οὔτε οὗτος ἥμαρτεν οὔτε οἱ γονεῖς αὐτοῦ, ἀλλ' ἵνα φανερωθῇ τὰ ἔργα τοῦ θεοῦ. The source marks the citation as John 3, which must be respected as a possible textual variation or conflation.

pass_b_english: When Christ was asked about this error, he was saying: "Neither this man sinned nor his parents, but this happened so that the works of God might be revealed" (John 3).

last_rejected.source_quote: ἀλλ' ἵνα φανερωθῇ τὰ ἔργα θεοῦ
last_rejected.why: Adds 'this happened' not in source; Greek has only 'but so that the works of God might be revealed'.
last_rejected.fix: Neither this man sinned nor his parents, but that the works of God might be revealed.
last_rejected.ruling: 'this happened' is standard English idiom rendering ἵνα purpose clause; no meaning changed or added
